report:
Oral cavity, left lateral tongue, partial glossectomy

Received in formalin is a partial glossectomy specimen measuring 45 x 30 x 20 mm. The specimen is orientated: long suture lateral, short suture anterior. There is an ulcerated tumour in the left lateral tongue measuring 18 x 12 x 8 mm, 6 mm from the closest (deep) margin. The margins are inked. Representative sections are taken in 8 blocks.

Specimen and tumour
- Procedure: Partial glossectomy
- Tumour site: Tongue (anterior two thirds), left
- Tumour size: 18 mm (greatest dimension)

Microscopic findings
- Histologic type: Squamous cell carcinoma, conventional (keratinising)
- Histologic grade: G2, moderately differentiated
- Tumour histology:
  The tumour is a moderately differentiated keratinising squamous cell carcinoma, invading to a depth of 8 mm. Infiltrating nests and cords of atypical squamous cells show intercellular bridges and focal keratinisation, with moderate nuclear pleomorphism, in a desmoplastic stroma.
- Depth of invasion: 8 mm
- Tumour extent: No extension beyond the primary site
- Lymphovascular invasion: Not identified
- Perineural invasion: Not identified

Margins
- Invasive tumour: All margins negative
  - Closest margin: 6 mm (deep)
- High grade dysplasia / carcinoma in situ: Margins uninvolved

Pathological stage (AJCC 8th edition)
- pTNM: pT2 pNX

Additional findings
- None identified

ORAL CAVITY, left lateral tongue, partial glossectomy
- SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA, moderately differentiated, 18 mm, invading to a depth
  of 8 mm; completely excised (closest margin 6 mm, deep); see synoptic report
- pT2 pNX (AJCC 8th edition)
